Q0036

“A multitude of books distracts; since you cannot read all you have,…” — Seneca (Letters to Lucilius, Ep. 2.2–4)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Letters to Lucilius, Ep. 2.2–4. Theme: philosophy.

Quotes / Seneca / Q0036

English

A multitude of books distracts; since you cannot read all you have, it is enough to have as much as you can read.
Thinker Seneca
School Stoicism
Source Letters to Lucilius, Ep. 2.2–4
Theme Philosophy
Another quotation More from this thinker

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Letters to Lucilius, Ep. 2.2–4 and files it under Stoicism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Seneca

Lucius Annaeus Seneca (c. 4 BCE–65 CE) was a Cordoban-born Stoic, tragic playwright, and adviser—later forced suicide victim—under Nero.
